newsitem.title: USA: America Online, Conn. reach agreement.
newsitem.headline: America Online, Conn. reach agreement.

text.p: Connecticut has reached an agreement with Internet service provider America Online over mounting consumer complaints about access to service, state officials said on Wednesday.
The agreement will give consumers the opportunity to receive a minimum refund of one month for the service problems experienced since the company began an unlimited service option last December 1.
The agreement was announced in a joint statement by Connecticut Attorney General Richard Blumenthal and Consumer Protection Commissioner Mark Shifrin.

Last Thursday, state attorneys general or their aides met in Chicago with Dulles, Va.-based America Online to discuss growing complaints in the past few months by consumers frustrated by repeated busy signals when they attempt to log on to the service.

America Online was hit by an unexpectedly large upsurge in the number of people trying to log on since December 1, when it switched its subscribers from an hourly pricing plan to a $19.95-a-month flat rate for unlimited access.
In trying to placate angry customers, the company has promised to spend $350 million to upgrade the service.
